criteria.evidence: Mostly holds. P05: the Charmaz 3rd edition (2024) was checked on the SAGE page; its chapter list (5 initial coding, 6 focused coding, 7 memo-writing, 8 theoretical sampling/saturation/sorting, 9 theorizing, 12 reflecting) matches sources.md, and recommender and decision authority are correctly none. P10: recommender (strategy_sponsor_or_design_team) is kept separate from decision_authority (accountable_decision_maker), and advise permits only conditional advice. P11: the Green Book 2026 edition was confirmed on GOV.UK (updated 5 Feb 2026). Recommendation (compare_advise) and decision (decide_feedback) are separate records, and prohibited edge c19 is in place. P12: consensus-as-truth is blocked by method_owned_rule and c19. P13: each strand has its own judgment owner and acceptance authority, and c23/c24 bar a single strand from licensing a meta-inference. AC1 fails on P12, where the judgment_owner default (individual_anonymous_panelists) is applied to the convener-owned design, feedback, interpretation and report moves. Source-locator and classification defects are listed below as should_fix.

P13 holds: divergence can return to align or to either strand (c15-c17), and unresolved divergence is a valid stopping point. P12 unrolls its Delphi feedback into three explicit rounds, each fed a controlled feedback packet (c05, c10). This is faithful to the frozen three-round variant, and u06 records why. AC2 fails on three methods. P05 drops the constant-comparison loop that the spec names as required, and its listed optional cycle is not closed by any connection. In P10 the futures-revision cycle has no connections behind it, and the strategy feedback edge carries a recommendation-typed output into a slot that expects options. P11 has no appraisal-return loop at all: the only feedback runs after the decision.
